Filings seek approval for new generation and transmission infrastructure to support growth while delivering benefits for existing customers

ASHLAND, Ky., Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Kentucky Power today filed plans with the Kentucky Public Service Commission (PSC) to bring significant new economic development to eastern Kentucky while delivering direct financial benefits to existing customers and protecting them from the costs of serving new large-load customers.

The filings would support TeraWulf's planned Muskie Data Campus in Grayson, Kentucky, and the infrastructure needed to serve it. Over the life of the agreement, the project is expected to provide Kentucky Power customers with more than $500 million in fixed-cost rate offsets and $100 million in winter bill credits for residential customers.

"Our commitment to eastern Kentucky goes beyond providing reliable electricity. We've served these communities for generations, and we want our customers and communities to share directly in the benefits when new investment comes to the region," said Cindy Wiseman, president and chief operating officer of Kentucky Power. "Eastern Kentucky has a tremendous opportunity ahead, and thoughtful growth can strengthen our electric system, support good jobs and attract new investment."

Supporting eastern Kentucky's economic growth

Kentucky Power announced its amended agreement with TeraWulf in October, and today's filings mark the next step in seeking the regulatory approvals needed to move the project forward.

TeraWulf's planned Muskie Data Campus is expected to support up to 1 gigawatt of contracted electric demand in phases by 2029, subject to regulatory approval and construction schedules. To reliably serve that demand, Kentucky Power is seeking approval to construct a new 760-MW combined-cycle natural gas facility next to its Big Sandy natural gas generating unit in Louisa and a new transmission substation in the EastPark Industrial Park area.

The planned Muskie Data Campus also is expected to generate new economic activity through infrastructure investment, construction activity, permanent jobs and new tax revenue for local communities.

Delivering benefits for existing customers

If approved by the PSC, TeraWulf will fund $100 million in winter bill credits for Kentucky Power's residential customers beginning in 2029 and continuing over the first 10 years of the contract.

Kentucky Power signed the White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge, reaffirming its commitment that growth should pay for growth while delivering long-term value for existing customers. Additionally, Kentucky Power's large-load tariff requires data centers to provide financial backing for the cost to serve their projects before they connect to the grid. 

In addition to paying all applicable service charges, TeraWulf has agreed to pay the estimated financing costs associated with construction of the proposed generation facility at Big Sandy. Together, these protections are designed to ensure the costs associated with serving TeraWulf's new demand are paid for by TeraWulf, while allowing new and existing customers to share in the benefits created by the growth.

Today's filings begin the next phase of regulatory review for the proposed agreement and infrastructure. The generation facility and transmission infrastructure each require separate Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity from the PSC. Subject to the PSC's review schedule, decisions on the filings could come as early as mid-year 2027. 

About Kentucky Power
Kentucky Power, with headquarters in Ashland, provides electric service to about 162,000 customers in 20 eastern Kentucky counties, including Boyd, Breathitt, Carter, Clay, Elliott, Floyd, Greenup, Johnson, Knott, Lawrence, Leslie, Letcher, Lewis, Magoffin, Martin, Morgan, Owsley, Perry, Pike and Rowan. Kentucky Power is an operating company in the American Electric Power (Nasdaq: AEP) system. For more information, visit kentuckypower.com.

BATON ROUGE, La.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--As Baton Rouge gets ready for the Texas-LSU matchup, Bloom Energy is joining the community off the field to support two organizations making a difference for families across Louisiana.

On Friday, Bloom Energy visited Baton Rouge Fire Station 12 to recognize the work of the Baton Rouge Area Foundation and Civic Collaborative Foundation, two organizations helping strengthen communities and support Louisianans in times of need. As part of the event, Bloom Energy presented each organization with a $10,000 donation.

“Keeping communities safe depends on the people and organizations that strengthen them every day,” said Natalie Sunderland, Chief Marketing Officer at Bloom Energy. “For decades, the Baton Rouge Area Foundation and Civic Collaborative Foundation have stood alongside Louisiana families and helped communities rebuild and move forward. We’re proud to support their work and the lasting resilience they’re building across Baton Rouge and South Louisiana.”

“We’re so thankful for Bloom Energy’s generosity in Baton Rouge, and for the tireless dedication of first responders everywhere,” said Chris Meyer, president and CEO of the Baton Rouge Area Foundation and Civic Collaborative Foundation. “This grant will allow our community to better prepare for disasters before they happen and equip the brave men and women of the Baton Rouge Fire Department to respond more effectively.”

Among the largest community foundations in the country, the Baton Rouge Area Foundation seeks to improve the quality of life in greater Baton Rouge and across south Louisiana by supporting local nonprofits, engaging community leaders and partnering with others to create positive regional change.

Civic Collaborative Foundation, a Baton Rouge-based nonprofit that shares leadership and administrative support with the Baton Rouge Area Foundation, provides temporary relief to individuals and families facing financial hardship after natural and man-made disasters along the Gulf Coast and helps Louisiana communities prepare for and recover from disasters.

The donations reflect Bloom Energy’s commitment to supporting the communities it serves and partnering with local organizations that are helping build stronger, more resilient communities.

Bloom will also be on campus Saturday ahead of the Texas-LSU game as ESPN Radio’s College Football Campus Tour powered by Bloom Energy brings its live broadcast and interactive Fan Zone to Baton Rouge.

Based on VOLGA Phase III trial data which showed a 49% reduction in risk of recurrence and a 42% reduction in risk of death, with a manageable safety profile

Approval reinforces potential of IMFINZI as an immunotherapy backbone across muscle-invasive and non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer​

WILMINGTON, Del.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--AstraZeneca’s ​IMFINZI® (durvalumab)​ in combination with enfortumab vedotin-ejfv (EV) as neoadjuvant treatment, followed by IMFINZI monotherapy as adjuvant treatment after radical cystectomy (surgery to remove the bladder), has been approved in the US for the treatment of adult patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) who are ineligible for or have refused cisplatin-based chemotherapy.

The approval was granted by the Food and Drug Administration after securing Priority Review and was based on results from the VOLGA Phase III trial which were presented during a Presidential Symposium at the 2026 European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress and simultaneously published in The New England Journal of Medicine.

In 2026, around 16,000 patients will be treated for MIBC in the United States.1 Approximately one in four patients with bladder cancer has muscle-invasive disease, where the tumor invades the muscle wall of the bladder, without distant metastases.2,3 As many as 50% of patients are ineligible for cisplatin-based chemotherapy due to impaired renal function or comorbidities.4,5 The standard treatment for these patients has historically been radical cystectomy alone, but despite undergoing this major surgery, patients experience high rates of recurrence and have a poor prognosis.4-6

Jonathan E. Rosenberg, MD, Chief of the Genitourinary Oncology Service at the Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center and member of the VOLGA Steering Committee, said: “This approval brings the first perioperative immunotherapy regimen where enfortumab vedotin-ejfv is administered only in the neoadjuvant setting to patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer who are not candidates for cisplatin-based chemotherapy. The results of VOLGA show a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in both event-free and overall survival along with a manageable safety profile. Based on this, the VOLGA regimen has the potential to become a new standard of care in this curative-intent setting.”

Dave Fredrickson, Executive Vice President, Oncology Haematology Business Unit, AstraZeneca, said: “Today's approval offers a novel IMFINZI-based regimen that almost halved the risk of disease recurrence and reduced the risk of death by 42 percent in the VOLGA trial, allowing physicians to optimize treatment for patients in this curative-intent setting. As our third bladder cancer indication in two years, this approval reinforces IMFINZI as an immunotherapy backbone across muscle-invasive and non-muscle-invasive disease.”

In the trial, patients were treated with three cycles of IMFINZI and EV before radical cystectomy, followed by nine cycles of IMFINZI adjuvant monotherapy. In a planned interim analysis, perioperative IMFINZI plus neoadjuvant EV demonstrated a 49% reduction in the risk of disease progression, recurrence, not undergoing surgery or death versus radical cystectomy with or without approved adjuvant treatment (based on an event-free survival [EFS] hazard ratio [HR] of 0.51; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.38-0.67; p<0.0001). Estimated median EFS was not yet reached for the IMFINZI combination versus 12.1 months for the comparator arm. An estimated 64% of patients treated with the IMFINZI combination remained alive and event-free at two years compared to 45% in the comparator arm.

Results from the key secondary endpoint of overall survival (OS) showed that the IMFINZI combination reduced the risk of death by 42% compared to the comparator arm (based on an OS HR of 0.58; 95% CI 0.40-0.83; p=0.0027). Estimated median OS was not yet reached for the IMFINZI combination or comparator arm. An estimated 78% of patients treated with the IMFINZI combination were alive at two years compared to 69% in the comparator arm.

The safety and tolerability of IMFINZI plus EV was consistent with the known safety profiles of the individual medicines, with no new safety signals identified. Grade 3 and 4 adverse events due to any cause occurred in 64% of patients treated with the IMFINZI combination and 44% of patients in the comparator arm. Patient-reported quality of life was maintained after surgery in patients treated with the IMFINZI combination.

Regulatory applications are currently under review in the European Union (EU), Japan and several other countries based on the results of the VOLGA trial.

IMFINZI is approved in over 50 countries for patients with cisplatin-eligible MIBC based on the NIAGARA Phase III trial. IMFINZI in combination with Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) induction and maintenance therapy is approved in the US, Japan and other countries for patients with BCG-naïve, high-risk non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer, based on the POTOMAC Phase III trial. In July 2026, positive high-level results from the NILE Phase III trial showed IMFINZI plus chemotherapy demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in OS versus chemotherapy as 1st-line treatment for patients with PD-L1 high unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

There are no contraindications for IMFINZI® (durvalumab) or IMJUDO® (tremelimumab-actl).

Severe and Fatal Immune-Mediated Adverse Reactions
Important immune-mediated adverse reactions listed under Warnings and Precautions may not include all possible severe and fatal immune-mediated reactions. Immune-mediated adverse reactions, which may be severe or fatal, can occur in any organ system or tissue. Immune-mediated adverse reactions can occur at any time after starting treatment or after discontinuation. Monitor patients closely for symptoms and signs that may be clinical manifestations of underlying immune-mediated adverse reactions. Evaluate clinical chemistries including liver enzymes, creatinine, adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) level, and thyroid function at baseline and before each dose. In cases of suspected immune-mediated adverse reactions, initiate appropriate workup to exclude alternative etiologies, including infection. Institute medical management promptly, including specialty consultation as appropriate. Withhold or permanently discontinue IMFINZI and IMJUDO depending on severity. See USPI Dosing and Administration for specific details. In general, if IMFINZI and/or IMJUDO requires interruption or discontinuation, administer systemic corticosteroid therapy (1 mg to 2 mg/kg/day prednisone or equivalent) until improvement to Grade 1 or less. Upon improvement to Grade 1 or less, initiate corticosteroid taper and continue to taper over at least 1 month. Consider administration of other systemic immunosuppressants in patients whose immune-mediated adverse reactions are not controlled with corticosteroid therapy.

Immune-Mediated Pneumonitis
IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause immune-mediated pneumonitis, which may be fatal. The incidence of pneumonitis is higher in patients who have received prior thoracic radiation.

  • IMFINZI as a Single Agent
    • In patients who did not receive recent prior radiation, the incidence of immune-mediated pneumonitis was 2.4% (34/1414), including fatal (<0.1%), and Grade 3-4 (0.4%) adverse reactions.
    • In patients who received recent prior radiation, the incidence of pneumonitis (including radiation pneumonitis) in patients with unresectable Stage III NSCLC following definitive chemoradiation within 42 days prior to initiation of IMFINZI in PACIFIC was 18.3% (87/475) in patients receiving IMFINZI and 12.8% (30/234) in patients receiving placebo. Of the patients who received IMFINZI (475), 1.1% were fatal and 2.7% were Grade 3 adverse reactions.
    • The incidence of pneumonitis (including radiation pneumonitis) in patients with LS-SCLC following chemoradiation within 42 days prior to initiation of IMFINZI in ADRIATIC was 14% (37/262) in patients receiving IMFINZI and 6% (16/265) in patients receiving placebo. Of the patients who received IMFINZI (262), 0.4% had a fatal adverse reaction and 2.7% had Grade 3 adverse reactions.
    • The frequency and severity of immune-mediated pneumonitis in patients who did not receive definitive chemoradiation prior to IMFINZI were similar in patients who received IMFINZI as a single agent or with ES-SCLC or BTC when given in combination with chemotherapy.
  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO
    • Immune‑mediated pneumonitis occurred in 1.3% (5/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO, including fatal (0.3%) and Grade 3 (0.2%) adverse reactions.
  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
    • Immune-mediated pneumonitis occurred in 3.5% (21/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy, including fatal (0.5%), and Grade 3 (1%) adverse reactions.

Immune-Mediated Colitis
IMFINZI with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy can cause immune-mediated colitis, which may be fatal. IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause immune-mediated colitis that is frequently associated with diarrhea. Cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection/reactivation has been reported in patients with corticosteroid-refractory immune-mediated colitis. In cases of corticosteroid-refractory colitis, consider repeating infectious workup to exclude alternative etiologies.

  • IMFINZI as a Single Agent
    • Immune-mediated colitis occurred in 2% (37/1889) of patients receiving IMFINZI, including Grade 4 (<0.1%) and Grade 3 (0.4%) adverse reactions.
  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO
    • Immune‑mediated colitis or diarrhea occurred in 6% (23/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO, including Grade 3 (3.6%) adverse reactions. Intestinal perforation has been observed in other studies of IMFINZI and IMJUDO.
  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
    • Immune-mediated colitis occurred in 6.5% (39/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy including fatal (0.2%) and Grade 3 (2.5%) adverse reactions. Intestinal perforation and large intestine perforation were reported in 0.1% of patients.

Immune-Mediated Hepatitis
IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause immune-mediated hepatitis, which may be fatal.

  • IMFINZI as a Single Agent
    • Immune-mediated hepatitis occurred in 2.8% (52/1889) of patients receiving IMFINZI, including fatal (0.2%), Grade 4 (0.3%), and Grade 3 (1.4%) adverse reactions.
  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO
    • Immune‑mediated hepatitis occurred in 7.5% (29/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO, including fatal (0.8%), Grade 4 (0.3%), and Grade 3 (4.1%) adverse reactions.
  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
    • Immune-mediated hepatitis occurred in 3.9% (23/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy, including fatal (0.3%), Grade 4 (0.5%), and Grade 3 (2%) adverse reactions.

Immune-Mediated Endocrinopathies

  • Adrenal Insufficiency: IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause primary or secondary adrenal insufficiency. For Grade 2 or higher adrenal insufficiency, initiate symptomatic treatment, including hormone replacement as clinically indicated.
    • IMFINZI as a Single Agent
      • Immune-mediated adrenal insufficiency occurred in 0.5% (9/1889) of patients receiving IMFINZI, including Grade 3 (<0.1%) adverse reactions.
    • IMFINZI with IMJUDO
      • Immune-mediated adrenal insufficiency occurred in 1.5% (6/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO, including Grade 3 (0.3%) adverse reactions.
    • IMFINZI with IMJUDO and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
      • Immune-mediated adrenal insufficiency occurred in 2.2% (13/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy, including Grade 3 (0.8%) adverse reactions.
  • Hypophysitis: IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause immune-mediated hypophysitis. Hypophysitis can present with acute symptoms associated with mass effect such as headache, photophobia, or visual field cuts. Hypophysitis can cause hypopituitarism. Initiate symptomatic treatment including hormone replacement as clinically indicated.
    • IMFINZI as a Single Agent
      • Grade 3 hypophysitis/hypopituitarism occurred in <0.1% (1/1889) of patients who received IMFINZI.
    • IMFINZI with IMJUDO
      • Immune-mediated hypophysitis/hypopituitarism occurred in 1% (4/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO.
    • IMFINZI with IMJUDO and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
      • Immune-mediated hypophysitis occurred in 1.3% (8/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy, including Grade 3 (0.5%) adverse reactions.
  • Thyroid Disorders: IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause immune-mediated thyroid disorders. Thyroiditis can present with or without endocrinopathy. Hypothyroidism can follow hyperthyroidism. Initiate hormone replacement therapy for hypothyroidism or institute medical management of hyperthyroidism as clinically indicated.
    • IMFINZI as a Single Agent
      • Immune-mediated thyroiditis occurred in 0.5% (9/1889) of patients receiving IMFINZI, including Grade 3 (<0.1%) adverse reactions.
      • Immune-mediated hyperthyroidism occurred in 2.1% (39/1889) of patients receiving IMFINZI.
      • Immune-mediated hypothyroidism occurred in 8.3% (156/1889) of patients receiving IMFINZI, including Grade 3 (<0.1%) adverse reactions.
    • IMFINZI with IMJUDO
      • Immune-mediated thyroiditis occurred in 1.5% (6/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO.
      • Immune-mediated hyperthyroidism occurred in 4.6% (18/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO, including Grade 3 (0.3%) adverse reactions.
      • Immune-mediated hypothyroidism occurred in 11% (42/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO.
    • IMFINZI with IMJUDO and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
      • Immune-mediated thyroiditis occurred in 1.2% (7/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy.
      • Immune-mediated hyperthyroidism occurred in 5% (30/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy, including Grade 3 (0.2%) adverse reactions.
      • Immune-mediated hypothyroidism occurred in 8.6% (51/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy, including Grade 3 (0.5%) adverse reactions.
    • IMFINZI with Carboplatin and Paclitaxel
      • Immune-mediated hypothyroidism occurred in 14% (34/235) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with carboplatin and paclitaxel.
  • Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus, which can present with diabetic ketoacidosis: Monitor patients for hyperglycemia or other signs and symptoms of diabetes. Initiate treatment with insulin as clinically indicated.
    • IMFINZI as a Single Agent
      • Grade 3 immune-mediated Type 1 diabetes mellitus occurred in <0.1% (1/1889) of patients receiving IMFINZI.
    • IMFINZI with IMJUDO
      • Two patients (0.5%, 2/388) had events of hyperglycemia requiring insulin therapy that had not resolved at last follow-up.
    • IMFINZI with IMJUDO and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
      • Immune-mediated Type 1 diabetes mellitus occurred in 0.5% (3/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy including Grade 3 (0.3%) adverse reactions.

Immune-Mediated Nephritis with Renal Dysfunction
IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause immune-mediated nephritis.

  • IMFINZI as a Single Agent
    • Immune-mediated nephritis occurred in 0.5% (10/1889) of patients receiving IMFINZI, including Grade 3 (<0.1%) adverse reactions.
  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO
    • Immune-mediated nephritis occurred in 1% (4/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO, including Grade 3 (0.5%) adverse reactions.
  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
    • Immune-mediated nephritis occurred in 0.7% (4/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy, including Grade 3 (0.2%) adverse reactions.

Immune-Mediated Dermatology Reactions
IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause immune-mediated rash or dermatitis. Exfoliative dermatitis, including Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS), drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS), and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), has occurred with PD-1/L-1 and CTLA-4 blocking antibodies. Topical emollients and/or topical corticosteroids may be adequate to treat mild to moderate non-exfoliative rashes.

  • IMFINZI as a Single Agent
    • Immune-mediated rash or dermatitis occurred in 1.8% (34/1889) of patients receiving IMFINZI, including Grade 3 (0.4%) adverse reactions.
  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO
    • Immune-mediated rash or dermatitis occurred in 4.9% (19/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO, including Grade 4 (0.3%) and Grade 3 (1.5%) adverse reactions.
  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
    • Immune-mediated rash or dermatitis occurred in 7.2% (43/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy, including Grade 3 (0.3%) adverse reactions.

Immune-Mediated Pancreatitis
IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO can cause immune-mediated pancreatitis. Immune-mediated pancreatitis occurred in 2.3% (9/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO, including Grade 4 (0.3%) and Grade 3 (1.5%) adverse reactions.

Other Immune-Mediated Adverse Reactions
The following clinically significant, immune-mediated adverse reactions occurred at an incidence of less than 1% each in patients who received IMFINZI and IMJUDO or were reported with the use of other immune-checkpoint inhibitors.

  • Cardiac/vascular: Myocarditis, pericarditis, vasculitis.
  • Nervous system: Meningitis, encephalitis, myelitis and demyelination, myasthenic syndrome/myasthenia gravis (including exacerbation), Guillain-Barré syndrome, nerve paresis, autoimmune neuropathy.
  • Ocular: Uveitis, iritis, and other ocular inflammatory toxicities can occur. Some cases can be associated with retinal detachment. Various grades of visual impairment to include blindness can occur. If uveitis occurs in combination with other immune-mediated adverse reactions, consider a Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada-like syndrome, as this may require treatment with systemic steroids to reduce the risk of permanent vision loss.
  • Gastrointestinal: Pancreatitis including increases in serum amylase and lipase levels, gastritis, duodenitis.
  • Musculoskeletal and connective tissue disorders: Myositis/polymyositis, rhabdomyolysis and associated sequelae including renal failure, arthritis, polymyalgia rheumatica.
  • Endocrine: Hypoparathyroidism.
  • Hematologic/Immune: Hemolytic anemia, aplastic anemia, hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, systemic inflammatory response syndrome, histiocytic necrotizing lymphadenitis (Kikuchi lymphadenitis), sarcoidosis, immune thrombocytopenia, solid organ transplant rejection, other transplant (including corneal graft) rejection.
  • Other: Myocarditis-Myositis-Myasthenia Gravis (or Myasthenia-Like) Overlap Syndrome, reported as the co-occurrence of either two or all three adverse reactions.

Infusion-Related Reactions
IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause severe or life-threatening infusion-related reactions. Monitor for signs and symptoms of infusion-related reactions. Interrupt, slow the rate of, or permanently discontinue IMFINZI and IMJUDO based on the severity. See USPI Dosing and Administration for specific details. For Grade 1 or 2 infusion-related reactions, consider using pre-medications with subsequent doses.

  • IMFINZI as a Single Agent
    • Infusion-related reactions occurred in 2.2% (42/1889) of patients receiving IMFINZI, including Grade 3 (0.3%) adverse reactions.
  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO
    • Infusion-related reactions occurred in 2.6% (10/388) of patients receiving IMFINZI and IMJUDO.
  • IMFINZI with IMJUDO and Platinum-Based Chemotherapy
    • Infusion-related reactions occurred in 2.9% (17/596) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy, including Grade 3 (0.3%) adverse reactions.
  • IMFINZI with Enfortumab Vedotin-ejfv (EV)
    • Infusion-related reactions occurred in 1.3% (3/228) of patients receiving IMFINZI in combination with EV.

Complications of Allogeneic HSCT after IMFINZI
Fatal and other serious complications can occur in patients who receive allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) before or after being treated with a PD-1/L-1 blocking antibody. Transplant-related complications include hyperacute graft-versus-host disease (GVHD), acute GVHD, chronic GVHD, hepatic veno-occlusive disease (VOD) after reduced intensity conditioning, and steroid-requiring febrile syndrome (without an identified infectious cause). These complications may occur despite intervening therapy between PD-1/L-1 blockade and allogeneic HSCT. Follow patients closely for evidence of transplant-related complications and intervene promptly. Consider the benefit versus risks of treatment with a PD-1/L-1 blocking antibody prior to or after an allogeneic HSCT.

Embryo-Fetal Toxicity
Based on their mechanism of action and data from animal studies, IMFINZI and IMJUDO can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman. Advise pregnant women of the potential risk to a fetus. In females of reproductive potential, verify pregnancy status prior to initiating IMFINZI and IMJUDO and advise them to use effective contraception during treatment with IMFINZI and IMJUDO and for 3 months after the last dose of IMFINZI and IMJUDO.

Lactation
There is no information regarding the presence of IMFINZI and IMJUDO in human milk; however, because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in breastfed infants from IMFINZI and IMJUDO, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose.

Indications:

IMFINZI, as a single agent, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with unresectable Stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose disease has not progressed following concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy and radiation therapy (cCRT).

IMFINZI in combination with platinum-containing chemotherapy as neoadjuvant treatment, followed by IMFINZI continued as a single agent as adjuvant treatment after surgery, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with resectable (tumors ≥4 cm and/or node positive) NSCLC and no known epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations or anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) rearrangements.

IMFINZI, in combination with IMJUDO and platinum-based chemotherapy, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic NSCLC with no sensitizing EGFR mutations or ALK genomic tumor aberrations.

IMFINZI, as a single agent, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with limited-stage small cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC) whose disease has not progressed following concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy and radiation therapy (cCRT).

IMFINZI, in combination with etoposide and either carboplatin or cisplatin, is indicated for the first-line treatment of adult patients with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC).

IMFINZI, in combination with gemcitabine and cisplatin, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract cancer (BTC).

IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC).

IMFINZI in combination with carboplatin and paclitaxel followed by IMFINZI as a single agent is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with primary advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer that is mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) as determined by an FDA-authorized test.

IMFINZI in combination with gemcitabine and cisplatin as neoadjuvant treatment, followed by single agent IMFINZI as adjuvant treatment following radical cystectomy, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC).

IMFINZI in combination with enfortumab vedotin-ejfv (EV) as neoadjuvant treatment, followed by single agent IMFINZI as adjuvant treatment after radical cystectomy, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with MIBC who are ineligible for or who have refused cisplatin-based chemotherapy.

IMFINZI in combination with fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin and docetaxel (FLOT) as neoadjuvant and adjuvant treatment, followed by single agent IMFINZI, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with resectable gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (GC/GEJC).

Notes

Bladder cancer
Bladder cancer is the 8th most common cancer in the world, with more than 635,000 cases diagnosed each year.7 The most common type is urothelial carcinoma, which begins in the urothelial cells of the urinary tract.8

In 2025, the NIAGARA Phase III trial established a new standard of care in MIBC by adding perioperative IMFINZI to neoadjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy and radical cystectomy.9 However, up to half of patients are not eligible to receive cisplatin, and approximately 50% of MIBC patients who undergo bladder removal surgery experience disease recurrence. New treatment options that prevent both progression before surgery and recurrence after surgery are critically needed in this curative-intent setting.4,6

VOLGA
VOLGA is a Phase III, randomized, open-label, multi-center global trial evaluating perioperative IMFINZI with or without tremelimumab-actl in combination with neoadjuvant EV as treatment for patients with MIBC undergoing radical cystectomy who are ineligible for or have refused cisplatin compared to radical cystectomy with or without approved adjuvant therapy. In the trial, 695 patients were randomized 1:1:1 to Arm 1 (three cycles of IMFINZI and EV, plus two cycles of tremelimumab-actl prior to surgery, followed by nine cycles of IMFINZI plus one cycle of tremelimumab-actl as adjuvant therapy), Arm 2 (three cycles of IMFINZI and EV prior to surgery, followed by nine cycles of IMFINZI adjuvant monotherapy) and Arm 3, the comparator arm.

The trial was conducted in 182 centers across 25 countries in Europe, North America, South America and Asia. Its dual primary endpoints are EFS, defined as the time from randomization to first recurrence post-radical cystectomy, first progression in patients who did not undergo radical cystectomy, failure to undergo radical cystectomy in patients with residual disease or death due to any cause, for both experimental arms versus the comparator arm. Secondary endpoints include OS (Arm 1 vs. Arm 3 and Arm 2 vs. Arm 3), pathologic complete response, disease-free survival and pathologic downstaging across both experimental arms.

IMFINZI® (durvalumab)
IMFINZI® (durvalumab) is a human monoclonal antibody that binds to the PD-L1 protein and blocks the interaction of PD-L1 with the PD-1 and CD80 proteins, countering the tumor's immune-evading tactics and releasing the inhibition of immune responses.

In addition to its bladder cancer indications, IMFINZI is the global standard of care based on OS in the curative-intent setting of unresectable, Stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in patients whose disease has not progressed after chemoradiotherapy (CRT). Additionally, IMFINZI is approved as a perioperative treatment in combination with neoadjuvant chemotherapy in resectable NSCLC, and in combination with a short course of IMJUDO® (tremelimumab-actl) and chemotherapy for the treatment of metastatic NSCLC. IMFINZI is also approved for limited-stage small cell lung cancer (SCLC) and in combination with chemotherapy (etoposide and either carboplatin or cisplatin) for the treatment of extensive-stage SCLC.

IMFINZI is also approved in combination with chemotherapy in locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract cancer and in combination with IMJUDO in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). It is also approved as a monotherapy in unresectable HCC in Japan, China and the EU, and in resectable, early-stage and locally advanced gastric and gastroesophageal junction cancers in the US, EU and Japan. Additionally, in April 2026, IMFINZI in combination with IMJUDO, lenvatinib and transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) demonstrated a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in the primary endpoint of progression-free survival versus TACE alone for patients with unresectable HCC eligible for embolization in the EMERALD-3 Phase III trial.

IMFINZI in combination with chemotherapy followed by IMFINZI monotherapy is approved as a 1st-line treatment for primary advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer (mismatch repair deficient disease only in the US, EU and China). IMFINZI in combination with chemotherapy followed by olaparib and IMFINZI is approved for patients with mismatch repair proficient advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer in the EU and Japan.

Since the first approval in May 2017, an estimated 600,000 patients have been treated with IMFINZI. As part of a broad development program, IMFINZI is being tested as a single treatment and in combinations with other anti-cancer treatments for patients with NSCLC, bladder cancer, breast cancer, ovarian cancer and several gastrointestinal cancers.

QUEBEC, QC / ACCESS Newswire / November 13, 2026 / NuRAN Wireless Inc. (NASDAQ:NUR)(FSE:1RN) ("NuRAN" or the "Company"), a provider of rural connectivity infrastructure in Africa, today announces that on November 10, 2026, it received a written notification letter (the "Notification Letter") from the Nasdaq Stock Market LLC ("Nasdaq") notifying NuRAN that it was not in compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2), as the minimum bid price of the Company's common shares ("Shares") has been below US$1.00 per share for 30 consecutive business days.

The Notification Letter is only a notification of deficiency and not a notice of delisting. As such, the Notification Letter has no immediate effect on the listing or trading of the Company's Shares on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol "NUR."

Nasdaq Listing Rules

Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) requires securities listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market to maintain a minimum bid price of US$1.00 per share, and Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A) provides that a failure to meet the minimum bid price requirement exists if the deficiency continues for a period of 30 consecutive business days. Based on the closing bid price of the Company's Shares for the 30 consecutive business days from September 29, 2026, to November 9, 2026, the Company has not met the minimum bid price requirement.

In accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A), NuRAN has a period of 180 calendar days, or until May 10, 2027, to regain compliance with the minimum bid price requirement. To regain compliance, the closing bid price of the Company's Shares must meet or exceed US$1.00 for at least ten consecutive business days during this 180-calendar day compliance period. Nasdaq may, in its discretion, require the Company to satisfy the minimum bid price requirement for a period of more than ten consecutive business days, generally not exceeding 20 consecutive business days, before determining that the Company has demonstrated an ability to maintain long-term compliance.

If the Company does not regain compliance by May 10, 2027, it may be eligible for an additional 180-calendar-day compliance period, provided that it meets the continued listing requirement for market value of publicly held shares (US$1 million) and all other initial listing standards for the Nasdaq Capital Market, other than the minimum bid price requirement. The Company must also provide written notice to Nasdaq of its intention to cure the deficiency during the additional compliance period, by effecting a reverse stock split, if necessary. If the Company elects to implement a reverse stock split, Nasdaq requires that it be completed no later than ten business days prior to the expiration of the initial 180-calendar-day compliance period ending May 10, 2027.

If it appears to Nasdaq that NuRAN will not be able to cure the deficiency, or if NuRAN is not otherwise eligible for additional time to regain compliance, the Company's Shares will be subject to delisting by Nasdaq. NuRAN may appeal any Nasdaq determination to delist its Shares, and during any appeal process, the Company's Shares would continue to trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market.

NuRAN's management intends to actively monitor the bid price for its Shares and will consider all available options to regain compliance with the Nasdaq minimum bid price requirement.

The Company's business operations are not affected by the receipt of the Notification Letter.

About NuRAN Wireless

NuRAN Wireless Inc. (Nasdaq:NUR)(FSE:1RN) is a rural telecommunications infrastructure company connecting remote and underserved communities across Africa. Through its Network-as-a-Service model, NuRAN finances, builds, owns, operates and maintains 2G, 3G and 4G mobile network infrastructure for mobile network operators seeking to expand coverage outside urban markets.

NuRAN has more than 5,000 towers under contract, a portion of which have been built and are operating. Its platform combines telecommunications engineering, low-power wireless technology, renewable-energy-enabled infrastructure, site selection and field operations to address the economic and technical challenges of rural mobile coverage.

NuRAN is also building on this foundation through NuEnergy, its wholly owned subsidiary focused on owning and operating the Company's solar, storage and hybrid power systems across its African footprint.

The Company is an intellectual property holding, investment, and commercialization company. We own and control a portfolio of intellectual property assets focused on the consumer sector, a legacy of our predecessor, Syms Corp. (“Syms”), including FilenesBasement.com, as well as the intellectual property associated with the Running of the Brides® event and the An Educated Consumer is Our Best Customer® slogan. Our strategy today centers on monetizing these assets through brand licensing, e-commerce initiatives, strategic partnerships, and protection and enforcement of our intellectual property rights.

Net Operating Losses

At September 30, 2026, the Company had carryforwards of federal net operating losses (“NOLs”) of approximately $352.8 million available to reduce future federal taxes. Of the Company’s federal NOLs, $224.5 million were generated prior to 2018 and may expire if unused by 2037, and $128.2 million were generated in 2018 and later years and can be carried forward indefinitely subject to an 80 percent taxable income annual limitation.

Based on management’s assessment, it is more likely than not that the deferred tax assets associated with the federal NOLs will not be realized by future taxable income or tax planning strategies. Accordingly, the Company has a valuation allowance of $74.1 million as of September 30, 2026. If our assumptions change and we determine that we will be able to realize these federal NOLs, the tax benefits relating to any reversal of the valuation allowance on deferred tax assets would be recognized as a reduction of income tax expense and an increase in the deferred tax asset.

Note that our certificate of incorporation includes a provision intended to help preserve certain tax benefits primarily associated with our NOLs. This provision generally prohibits, subject to certain exceptions, transfers of stock that would result in a person or group of persons becoming a 4.75 percent stockholder, or that would result in an increase or decrease in stock ownership by a person or group of persons that is an existing 4.75 percent stockholder.

VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Christina Lake Cannabis Corp. (the “Company” or “CLC”) (CSE: CLC) (OTCQB: CLCFF) (FRANKFURT: CLB) announces that its Board of Directors has appointed Nicco Dehaan, the Company’s co-founder and Chief Operating Officer, as Chief Executive Officer, effective November 13, 2026. Mr. Dehaan succeeds Mark Aiken, who is moving on to pursue other opportunities.

The appointment follows the Board’s decision, announced November 10, 2026, that CLC will remain independent and pursue its standalone plan: a sharper focus on the cultivation and sale of cannabis flower, lower costs, increased cultivation capacity and continued debt repayment. With that plan centred on CLC’s farms, the Board believes the Company is best led by the executive who built and runs them.

Mr. Dehaan co-founded CLC and has served as a director since 2019. As COO and Master Grower, he has overseen cultivation, processing and production across the Company’s Christina Lake and Midway properties and has worked closely on sales and product strategy. He will continue to serve as Chief Operating Officer and as a director.

“Having chosen to remain independent, our priority now is execution – getting the most out of the land, facilities and people we already have,” said Jay McMillan, Chairman of the Board. “Nicco knows this business from the ground up. He helped build it, and he led the operations behind our strong harvest this year. He is the right person to take CLC into its next phase. On behalf of the Board, I thank Mark for his leadership over the past four years, and wish him every success.”

“I’m proud to lead the company I helped found,” said Mr. Dehaan. “We have excellent land, proven infrastructure and a team that delivered a strong harvest this year. My priorities are clear: grow more high-quality flower from the assets we already own, keep costs down, continue paying down debt and build value for our shareholders. I look forward to working with our team and the Board to get it done.”

CLC is a licensed producer of cannabis under the Cannabis Act (Canada) with a standard cultivation licence and corresponding processing amendment from Health Canada as well as a research and development licence. "From advancing temporary and permanent worker housing to pioneering new access into the site, our Stibnite Gold Project is well positioned to move forward with disciplined execution. Our exploration drill program delivered compelling new mineralization, including multiple high-grade gold intervals and a new gold-tungsten discovery."

Webinar Update on Tuesday, November 17, 2026

Perpetua is pleased to announce that it will host a webinar on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, at 9:00 AM Mountain Time (11:00 AM Eastern Time). Third Quarter 2026 and Recent Highlights

  • Construction: Worker housing facility civil works were completed in late August 2026, and foundation installation commenced during the quarter. Work on the Burntlog Route ramped up through the summer field season, and long-lead powerline items have been ordered.
  • Exploration: The 2026 Exploration Drilling Program is complete, with more than 16,000 meters of core drilled. In August and then in November 2026, the Company reported new high-grade gold and antimony discoveries and identified a new gold-tungsten zone.
  • Financing update: Perpetua continued diligence and documentation on the $2.9 billion senior secured long-term loan from the Export-Import Bank of the United States ("U.S. EXIM") under the Make More in America Initiative, approved by the U.S. EXIM board on May 21, 2026. Closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027. The Company continues to advance detailed engineering, long-lead procurement, early works, critical path construction, and execution planning ahead of a final investment and construction decision. Unrestricted cash was $443.4 million as of September 30, 2026.
  • Antimony pilot plant: In July 2026, the Company commissioned a mobile modular processing plant, in partnership with Idaho National Laboratory, for pilot-scale testing to advance a secure domestic supply chain for antimony trisulfide.
  • Community: In July 2026, the Company opened a community resource and visitor information center in Yellow Pine, Idaho.

Construction Update

Perpetua completed 494,480 work hours during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, with no reportable spills and no serious injuries. Other highlights include:

  • Burntlog Route: Crews advanced construction along the alignment, removed dead timber left by past wildfires, and moved to pioneer roadwork. The year-round access road will give the Project an expanded and upgraded route capable of handling larger loads and equipment.
  • Worker Housing Facility: Treated wood foundations were installed for the kitchen, dining, and recreation modules, and a metal foundation was installed to support the dormitory buildings and the arctic corridor.
  • Powerline: Perpetua is well advanced in procuring key equipment. Substations and transformers are on order, while deliveries of power poles and ancillary equipment continue to the Company's laydown areas in Donnelly and Cascade, Idaho. Power pole installation commenced in October.

Looking ahead, Perpetua will continue to advance critical path work including bridge deliveries for Burntlog Route, installation of the worker housing facility, ongoing powerline procurement and construction, and placing orders for long-lead-time equipment.

New Exploration Results Announced

The 2026 drilling program sought to upgrade in-pit and near-pit inferred resources, extend mineralization along strike, test key underground targets, and follow up on discoveries from the 2025-2026 program. Recent highlights included:

  • Fiddle Discovery: The new Fiddle prospect, located approximately 750 meters south of the permitted Yellow Pine Pit, includes some of the most significant mineralized material encountered at the Stibnite Gold Project to date. Discovery hole SB633 returned 109.7 meters of 3.2 g/t gold and 1.1% antimony. Fiddle adds a new target area with potential to expand the Project's in-pit and near-pit resource base. The Company has since completed significant additional drilling at Fiddle, with assay results expected in the coming months.
  • Clark Tunnel Fault Zone (CTFZ): First announced in August, the CTFZ is located within or adjacent to the southeastern limits of the permitted Yellow Pine Pit. New results announced earlier this month returned near-surface, high-grade gold intercepts from recent drilling, including 25.4 meters of 4.5 g/t gold from 13 meters downhole and 25.0 meters of 2.3 g/t gold from 18 meters downhole. These results follow the drilling announced in August, which included a tungsten discovery in Hole SB597 that returned 21.3 meters of 3.2 g/t gold and 0.9% tungsten from 24 meters downhole.

Near-Term Outlook

Through the remainder of 2026 and early 2027, Perpetua is advancing early works, critical path construction, and detailed engineering for the process plant. Other initiatives include finalizing key construction and equipment contracts. With the 2026 exploration program recently completed, Perpetua expects to announce ongoing exploration results into 2027.

Perpetua Resources Corp., through its wholly owned subsidiaries, is focused on the exploration, site restoration and redevelopment of gold-antimony-silver deposits in the Stibnite-Yellow Pine district of central Idaho. The Stibnite Gold Project is one of the highest-grade, open-pit gold deposits in the United States and holds the only identified domestic reserve of the critical mineral antimony, which is essential to the defense, energy and manufacturing sectors. The Project is designed to apply a modern, responsible mining approach to restore a historic mine site and provide uplift to water quality, improve fish habitat access, and invest in river restoration while supporting local economic development in rural Idaho.

TORONTO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Organigram Global Inc. (NASDAQ: OGI) (TSX: OGI) (the “Company” or “Organigram”), Canada's #1 cannabis company by market share¹ and a growing global cannabis platform, today announced that on November 11, 2026, it received notification (the “Notification”) from The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq”) that it is not in compliance with the minimum bid price requirement under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5450(a)(1) for continued listing on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. The Notification was issued because the closing bid price of the Company's common shares was below US$1.00 per share for 30 consecutive business days. Nasdaq Listing Rule 5450(a)(1) requires listed common shares to maintain a minimum bid price of US$1.00 per share (the “Minimum Bid Requirement”), while Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A) provides that a deficiency exists when the requirement is not met for 30 consecutive business days.

The Notification has no immediate effect on the listing or trading of the Company's common shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. Pursuant to Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A), the Company has 180 calendar days, until May 10, 2027, to regain compliance with the Minimum Bid Requirement. To regain compliance, the closing bid price of the Company's common shares must be at least US$1.00 per share for a minimum of 10 consecutive business days during the compliance period, subject to Nasdaq's discretion to extend this period.

If the Company does not regain compliance by May 10, 2027, it may be eligible for an additional 180-calendar-day compliance period, subject to satisfying applicable Nasdaq requirements, including transferring its listing to the Nasdaq Capital Market. If the Company does not qualify for an additional compliance period, its common shares may become subject to delisting proceedings, subject to applicable appeal rights.

The Company's common shares are also listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange, and the Notification does not affect the Company's listing or compliance status on that exchange.

About Organigram

Organigram Global Inc. is listed on the NASDAQ Global Select Market and TSX. The Company's wholly owned subsidiary, Organigram Inc., is a licensed cultivator and processor. The facility in Aylmer houses best-in-class extraction capabilities, and is optimized for formulation refinement, post-processing of minor cannabinoids, and infused pre-roll production. The facility in London will be optimized for labelling, packaging, and national fulfillment. The Company is regulated by Health Canada under the Cannabis Act and the Cannabis Regulations.

HOUSTON, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- First Horizon Bank (NYSE: FHN) (or "First Horizon") today announced it is working alongside Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of Galveston-Houston and AltCap to implement an innovative financing solution to build a new 60,000-square-foot facility that will significantly improve access to food and other services for low-income Houstonians. The new Family Opportunity Center in north Houston will leverage New Markets Tax Credits (NMTC) provided by First Horizon Bank and the Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) AltCap.

Slated to open its doors in 2028, the Family Opportunity Center will feature a market-style food pantry, thrift store, and access to the nonprofit's services, including mental health counseling, parenting classes, rental assistance and job readiness resources. It will also provide space for community and first responders during natural disasters, along with ample warehouse space for food storage.

The total investment for the center, located at 9111 Jensen Drive, is $25 million. To date, Catholic Charities has raised $17.5 million in private and foundation gifts. The NMTC represents nearly 10 percent of the total needed.

Congress established the NMTC to encourage private-sector investment in low-income communities, including the future location of the Family Opportunity Center. Under the program, CDFIs such as AltCap are awarded tax credit allocations from the U.S. Department of the Treasury and deploy them to support projects that deliver measurable community benefits. Investors, including financial institutions like First Horizon Bank, receive federal tax credits in exchange for qualified investments. This investment structure enables community-serving projects, such as the Family Opportunity Center, to access favorable financing and move forward when traditional financing alone may be insufficient.

"We are proud to work alongside Catholic Charities and AltCap to provide financing for the Family Opportunity Center," said Yasmin Huebinger, Houston Commercial Banking Leader for First Horizon Bank. "This investment reflects First Horizon's commitment to strengthening the communities we serve, expanding economic opportunities and driving sustainable growth that benefits families and the broader Houston community."

"As Catholic Charities continues its Building to Serve Capital Campaign, the Family Opportunity Center stands as a testament to what can be achieved when nonprofit organizations, community development partners and financial institutions align resources around a shared vision," said Michael D. Hansen, president and CEO of Catholic Charities. "The cooperation among Catholic Charities, AltCap and First Horizon Bank illustrates how innovative financing can help transform lives and strengthen communities across the Houston region."

"As a CDFI that has been helping to increase access to capital for Houston entrepreneurs and small businesses since 2022, AltCap is excited to demonstrate how we can also support high impact community investments like the Family Opportunity Center using the NMTC Program," said Ruben Alonso III, CEO of AltCap. "We look forward to continuing to bring capital and other resources to underserved communities and small businesses throughout Houston as well as Harris County." 

The Catholic Charities Family Opportunity Center is AltCap's first NMTC investment in Texas. Since its founding, AltCap has deployed nearly $350 million in capital, from microloans to NMTC financing, to entrepreneurs and communities often overlooked and underserved by traditional financial institutions.

For more information about Catholic Charities' Family Opportunity Center, visit the Catholic Charities website.

About Catholic Charities 
Catholic Charities of the Archdiocese of Galveston-Houston brings help and hope to people in need, especially the poor and vulnerable. Through a network of life-changing programs that work together to alleviate poverty, we serve thousands of people each year from locations in Harris, Fort Bend and Galveston counties. Key Terms

reitfinancial
A real estate investment trust (REIT) is a company that owns, operates, or finances income-producing real estate, like shopping centers, apartments, or office buildings. They function like a mutual fund for real estate, making it easier for people to add property investments to their portfolio.
triple net leasefinancial
A triple net lease is a rental agreement where the tenant pays the base rent plus three main ongoing costs: property taxes, building insurance, and routine maintenance. For investors, this shifts much of the expense and risk onto the tenant, creating a steadier, more predictable income stream for the property owner—similar to renting a furnished home where the renter also pays the bills—making valuation and cash-flow forecasting simpler.
ebitdafinancial
EBITDA stands for earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization. It measures a company's profitability by focusing on the money it makes from its core operations, ignoring expenses like taxes and accounting adjustments. Investors use EBITDA to compare how well different companies are performing financially, as it provides a clearer picture of operational success without the influence of financial structure or accounting choices.
